To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) if there is no t, then the only failure detector that suffices to achieve UDC is a perfect failure detector; (2) if there is t, then a generalized failure detector suffices to achieve the same; and (3) the generalized failure detector can be implemented using a combination of a perfect failure detector and a perfect failure detector with bounded accuracy.

(1) UDC can be attained if the number of faulty processors is bounded and there exists a certain type of failure detector; (2) UDC cannot be attained if the failure detector is not strong enough; and (3) UDC cannot always be attained if there is no upper bound on the number faulty processors and the failure detector is perfect.

(i) in systems with unreliable communication, if there is a bound on the number (t) of faulty processes, UDC is possible if and only if the system has perfect failure detection, and (ii) if there is no such bound, UDC is not possible even if the system has a perfect failure detector.
